newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH MPS WANT TO ENSURE ECB POLICY LEGITIMATENESS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH MPS WANT TO ENSURE ECB POLICY LEGITIMATENESS.

text.p: Finland may need a national council to discuss the monetary policy objectives of Europe's new central bank (ECB) and the stance of the Finnish central bank's representative in ECB decision-making, a parliamentary committee said in a statement received on Tuesday.

In its response to a government proposal to reform Bank of Finland legislation, the assembly's economic committee also voiced views on the planned third stage of European economic and monetary union, which was not directly touched by the proposal.
The committee said a "national stability council" might be necessary to ensure the legitimateness of ECB monetary policy.
"Particularly considering the third stage there is reason to also consider the legitimateness of monetary policy, or how the objectives are anchored in society," the committee said.

The representative of the Bank of Finland's board of management would, while taking part in ECB decision-making, act outside the sphere of national political decision-making and unconnected with the national society at large "in a way which could endanger the legitimateness of monetary policy," it said.
This would apply if Finland participated in the third stage of EMU, the committee noted.

The proposed national stability council would "discuss the European central bank's monetary policy and the key objectives based on which the Bank of Finland will participate in the European central bank system's decision-making," the committee said.

It said the European monetary institute (EMI) -- the forerunner to the ECB, which is due to be set up in mid-1998 -- had last year interpreted the Maastricht treaty's clause on central bank indepencence so that discussions between national central banks and political decision-makers should not be prohibited.
